_doc: UNKNOWNS-1 (Rowan, 2026-11-17): what the system does not know is a core feedback loop, not a side task. Improving only what is known shrinks the solution space; this loop keeps it growing by questioning the system itself. Method sources: Universal Ignorance Audit (Rowan, Sciforum 35457 and QNFO/ignorance-audit: fifteen questions in five phases, three regions known unknowns / unknown unknowns / ignorance about ignorance, categories scaffold, map-territory, protected ignorance, the last answer seeds the next pass, separated roles, 'we do not know' is a normal outcome), Rumsfeld/Johari matrix, assumption audit, inversion and pre-mortem (Klein), red teaming. `python3 -m foundation unknowns --run --apply` inventories every loop and blind-spot need, generates inverted questions per lens, scores them, files the top ones as plus items (Q-UNK-*) and records every step in the append-only ledger ops/unknowns/ledger.jsonl (the provenance record). `--answer` closes a question with evidence; a gap or new objective is appended to ops/unknowns/objective-candidates.json (probationary, read back by `--run` and by the product manager) and seeds the next pass (UIA rule 6).

lenses.q: Assume loop '{id}' has failed completely a month from now without anyone noticing. Write the most likely cause, then name what in the system would have detected it. If nothing would, that is the gap.
List every assumption that must be true for the done check '{done}' to mean the outcome really happened. Which has never been tested, and by what independent path could it be?
How could the closing probe '{probe}' pass while the real outcome is false (map and territory differ)? Build the case, then the probe that would catch it.
What does '{id}' never observe? Its trigger is '{trigger}'. Name one signal outside that trigger that would change what it does, and who or what already holds it.
What shields '{id}' from being questioned (a default, an SLA, a kill switch, a past success)? What would we ask if that shield did not exist?
Which questions about '{id}' have we never written down because the loop's own structure made them unaskable? Write three, then answer 'we do not know' where true.
